html:
The North West Company was a fur trading business based in Montreal from 1779 to 1821, the great rival of the Hudson's Bay Company for the furs of what is now western Canada.

It was a partnership of mostly Scottish merchants whose French Canadian voyageurs paddled big canoes from Montreal deep into Rupert's Land, which the Hudson's Bay Company claimed as its own.

Its men explored much of the north and west:

  • Alexander Mackenzie followed the Mackenzie River to the Arctic Ocean in 1789 and crossed to the Pacific in 1793.
  • Simon Fraser went down the Fraser River in 1808.
  • David Thompson set up Spokane House among the Spokane in 1810 and followed the Columbia to the sea in 1811.

The rivalry turned violent, with killings at Seven Oaks on the Red River in 1816, and in 1821 the two firms merged under the Hudson's Bay name. Many Iroquois, Cree and Métis families who had worked for the company, such as the Mountain Métis, stayed in the west.
sum: The North West Company was a fur trading business based in Montreal from 1779 to 1821, the great rival of the Hudson's Bay Company for the furs of what is now western Canada.
